title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche. Grothendieck studies automorphisms of the genus-0 profinite Teichmüller groupoid in low dimension.

- Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. It is free profinite on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1.
- Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a profinite extension of S_3 by Π̂_{0,3}, i.e. Π̂_{0,3} = Ker(Ŝ^+_{0,3} → S_3). It contains an involution σ_∞ (exchanging 0 and 1) and an order-3 element ρ (cycling 0, 1, ∞). The tilde versions adjoin complex conjugation τ_0.
- φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a homomorphism, distinct from the inclusion. By the previous page, its composite φ̂· to S_3 has kernel normally generated by l_0², l_1², l_∞³. So φ̂· factors through the (2,2,3) triangle quotient, which is S_3.
- M^{!~}_{0,3} is a group of automorphisms of the extended object.

Corollary 2 (this page). Consider the automorphisms u that commute 'extérieurement' (up to inner automorphisms) with φ̂ and with ρ. These correspond bijectively to pairs (ξ, f) in Π̂_{0,3} × Π̂_{0,3}, where ξ satisfies two conditions:
- (14) the 3-cycle (cocycle) relation ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ²(ξ) = 1;
- (15) a 2-cycle relation ξ = [φ̂(ξ)·σ_∞(φ̂(ξ))^{-1}]·l_1^ν, for some ν ∈ Ẑ with 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^*.

So λ = 2ν+1 plays the role of the cyclotomic exponent and ν = (λ−1)/2 is the familiar 'm' of Drinfeld's hexagon.

Consequences for such a ξ:
- φ̂·(ξ) lies in {1, σ_∞}, i.e. equals σ_∞^i. One sets β = φ̂(ξ)σ_∞^{∓i}, which lies in Π̂_{0,3}.
- α is the unique element of Π̂^~_{0,3} with α·ρ(α)^{-1} = ξ. This is a Hilbert-90 type trivialisation of the Z/3-cocycle given by (14).
- Then (17) gives u(σ_∞) = int(f^{-1})(βσ_∞β^{-1}) = int(f^{-1})(ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞) and u(ρ) = int(f^{-1})(αρα^{-1}) = int(f^{-1})(ξρ).

Consistency check. If φ̂(ξ) = βσ_∞^i, then φ̂(ξ)σ_∞φ̂(ξ)^{-1}σ_∞^{-1} = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}. Hence (15) says exactly that βσ_∞β^{-1} = ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞. Likewise αρα^{-1} = αρ(α)^{-1}ρ = ξρ.

The margin notes that α and β are actually superfluous: u is expressed directly in ξ, ν, f. The page ends by observing that f only enters through composition with int(f^{-1}). The next page writes this as u_{ξ,f} = int(f^{-1})∘u_ξ, with u_ξ commuting with φ̂ (Corollary 3).

In modern terms, this is a GT-style parametrisation (λ, f) of 'non-inner' automorphisms of a profinite extended modular/mapping-class group. It is derived from the 3-cycle and 2-cycle relations, and the inner part is split off.
errors: Not an error in substance, but (15) as written uses φ̂(ξ) ∈ Ŝ^+ rather than β. It is correct, since the σ_∞^i factor cancels in φ̂(ξ)σ_∞φ̂(ξ)^{-1}σ_∞^{-1}.
In (16), β = φ̂(ξ)σ_∞^i lies in Π̂_{0,3} only if the exponent sign is chosen to cancel φ̂·(ξ) = σ_∞^i. Since σ_∞ has order 2 in S_3 this is harmless.
'α ∈ Π̂_{0,3}' should read α ∈ Π̂^~_{0,3}, as Grothendieck himself specifies on the next line.
The uniqueness of α (with α·ρ(α)^{-1} = ξ) needs triviality of the relevant centraliser of ρ. This is asserted, not proved here; the margin itself says more 'vérification liminaire' is needed.
The next page's transcription of (18), u_ξ(σ_∞) = (ξ l_1^{-ν})^2 σ_∞, conflicts with (17) on this page, which gives ξ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞. Either the exponent is a misreading or it is an inconsistency.

ideas.what: Parametrisation of automorphisms commuting (up to inner) with the structure maps by pairs (ξ, f), with ξ satisfying a 3-cycle and a 2-cycle relation involving λ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^*
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ (pairs (λ, f) with 2-cycle, 3-cycle/hexagon relations); description of GT̂ as automorphisms of profinite braid/mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1994, GT̂ and automorphisms of braid groups); later Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki, Minamide–Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces the program of studying Aut of the Teichmüller tower; no explicit (λ, f) equations there

ideas.what: Writing a ρ-cocycle ξ (ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1) as a coboundary αρ(α)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary form of the 3-cycle relation (analogue of f = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y) for the 2-cycle relation)

ideas.what: Splitting off the inner part: u_{ξ,f} = int(f^{-1})∘u_ξ
Homomorphism φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} whose composite to S_3 kills l_0², l_1², l_∞³
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold covering map relating P^1−3 points to a (2,2,3)/(2,3,∞)-type orbifold

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently derives a GT-type parametrisation of automorphisms (with λ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^* and 2-cycle/3-cycle relations on ξ) via automorphisms of an extended profinite genus-0 group commuting with an auxiliary map φ̂. This predates or parallels Drinfeld and Lochak–Schneps.
missed.quote: correspondent biunivoquement aux couples (ξ, f) ... (14) ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 (15) ξ = (φ̂(ξ)σ_∞(φ̂(ξ))^{-1}) l_1^ν (ν ∈ Ẑ convenable tel que 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own route to GT̂. The role of φ̂ (an equivariance with respect to a non-standard orbifold map) is a characterisation by commutation with φ̂ that does not obviously appear in the GT literature. It might give an alternative definition of GT̂ or a variant.

missed.claim: The margin admits the needed preliminary verifications (existence and uniqueness of α, well-definedness) are not done.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; these are now known-type lemmas.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a concrete unpublished derivation of GT-like equations by Grothendieck, with a distinctive formulation via commutation with φ̂ and ρ. It is a notable detail, but GT itself and its interpretation as automorphisms of profinite mapping class groups are well established. Grothendieck's general priority is also known to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Pour un tel ξ, φ̂(ξ) dans S_3' should be 'φ̂·(ξ) dans S_3'; the dot is visible in the image, matching (12)-(13) of the previous page.
The range of i: the image reads 'ℤ/12ℤ' or 'ℤ/2ℤ'; either way only i mod 2 matters, since σ_∞ has order 2 in S_3.
'Contrôle?' is underlined at the top; it may read 'Corollaire 2', which the next page cites as 'en termes du Corollaire 2'.
Second margin note: 'en fait, on n'a pas besoin de α, β (16)'.
